findings.title: One-second counter breaks existing 60-second backstop e2e case
findings.section: Task 14 - The music-font clock, and AlphaTab's own error event (Step 3, the end-to-end assertions)
findings.why_it_matters: The existing end-to-end case 'a music font that arrives after the 60 s backstop clears the error' (web/e2e/player.e2e.ts:230) goes red after this task, while Step 3 tells the implementer it passes. That case jumps the page clock with `page.clock.fastForward(61_000)`, and the installed Playwright 1.61.1 documents that call as firing due timers 'at most once', so Choice 7's one-second counter (the E204 clock; E204 is the 60-second music-font timeout) gains one second per jump, not sixty, and cannot reach 60 inside the case's 20-second retry window. The result is an unexplained failure in a merge-blocking lane, with no step naming which side to change. Advancing the fake clock with `page.clock.runFor(61_000)` fires the tick sixty-one times, so Choice 7 and the unit tests stand as written.
findings.suggested_fix: In Task 14 Step 3, add an edit to the existing case 'a music font that arrives after the 60 s backstop clears the error' in web/e2e/player.e2e.ts: inside its `toPass` block replace `await page.clock.fastForward(61_000);` with `await page.clock.runFor(61_000);`, keep the rest of the case, and change the 'Expected' sentence to say that this case is edited because `fastForward` fires an interval at most once.

findings.title: Render-finished unit test throws on its own stand-in api
findings.section: Task 14 - The music-font clock, and AlphaTab's own error event (Step 1, the 'once a render has finished' test)
findings.why_it_matters: The 'once a render has finished, hiding and showing the tab raises nothing a minute later' case throws before it asserts anything. Its stand-in api is `{}`, and the component's renderFinished handler (web/app/play/NotationSurface.tsx:166) ends with `setRenderedTrackCount(api?.tracks.length ?? 0)`; the `?.` guards only `api`, so `{}.tracks.length` raises a TypeError that escapes `act` and fails the case. Step 2's 'Expected: PASS — 6 tests' is therefore wrong, and the spec's promise that a finished render stops the clock for good has no passing test. Adding `tracks: []` to the stand-in fixes it; the alternative of loosening the production line to `api?.tracks?.length` is rejected because it would put a test accommodation into shipped code.
findings.suggested_fix: In Task 14 Step 1, change `const STAND_IN_API: unknown = {};` to `const STAND_IN_API: unknown = { tracks: [] };` and extend the comment above it to say the component reads `api.tracks.length` when a render finishes.

findings.title: Step 8's 'undo the same way' discards the home-page copy
findings.section: Task 7 - The three error pages, and the copy (Step 8, look at the three error pages, item 3)
findings.why_it_matters: Following Step 8 literally loses the new home-page copy. By then `web/app/page.tsx` holds Step 6's uncommitted tagline and privacy paragraph, and 'Undo it the same way' for item 3 means `git checkout -- web/app/page.tsx`, which restores the file to HEAD and discards both. Step 9 then commits the regenerated `landing-chromium-linux.png` (showing the new copy) beside a page that no longer has it, so the `web` visual-regression job fails at the landing shot, and Step 8's 'git status is clean' check cannot reveal it. Items 1 and 4 touch files nothing earlier edited, so only item 3 needs a different undo.
